question.text: Simplify the following sentence: "The bike is blue or the bike is green, or the bike is green and it is a green bike."
question.choice1: The bike is blue or green
question.choice3: The bike is blue and green
question.choice4: The bike is blue but not green
question.explanation:
First, we simplify the phrase "the bike is green and it is a green bike" to just "the bike is green." The sentence now reads

"The bike is blue or the bike is green, or the bike is green."

Then, using the associative law, we can move the comma in the sentence:

"The bike is blue, or the bike is green or the bike is green."

Now, we simplify the phrase "the bike is green or the bike is green" to just "the bike is green." The sentence now reads

"the bike is blue or the bike is green."

Finally, we simplify the sentence to

"The bike is blue or green."

exampleAnswers.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Associative Law

question.text: Simplify $(M \lor N) \lor N.$
question.explanation:
Using the associative and idempotent laws, we get

\[ \begin{align*} (M \lor N) \lor N &\equiv M \lor (N \lor N)\\[5pt] &\equiv M \lor N. \end{align*} \]

example.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Associative Law

question.text: Simplify $A \land (A \land B).$
question.explanation:
Using the associative and idempotent laws, we get

\[ \begin{align*} A \land (A \land B) &\equiv (A \land A) \land B\\[5pt] &\equiv A \land B. \end{align*} \]

example.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Associative Law

question.text: Simplify $(M \land N) \land (N \lor N).$
question.explanation:
Using the associative and idempotent laws, we get

\[ \begin{align*} (M \land N) \land (N \lor N) &\equiv(M \land N) \land N \\[5pt] &\equiv M \land (N \land N) \\[5pt] &\equiv M \land N. \end{align*} \]

example.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Associative Law

question.text: Simplify $P \land (( P \land Q) \land Q).$
question.explanation:
Using the associative and idempotent laws, we get

\begin{align*} P \land (( P \land Q) \land Q) &\equiv P \land ( P \land (Q \land Q))\\[5pt] &\equiv P \land ( P \land Q) \\[5pt] &\equiv (P \land P) \land Q \\[5pt] &\equiv P \land Q. \end{align*}

example.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Associative Law

question.text: Simplify $(A \lor A) \land (A \land B).$
question.explanation:
Using the associative and idempotent laws, we get

\[ \begin{align*} (A \lor A) \land (A \land B) &\equiv A \land (A \land B) \\[5pt] &\equiv (A \land A) \land B \\[5pt] &\equiv A \land B. \end{align*} \]

exampleAnswers.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Commutative Law

question.text: Which expression is equivalent to $(P \land M) \lor Q?$
question.explanation:
By the commutative law, $P \land M \equiv M \land P.$

Therefore, $(P \land M) \lor Q \equiv (M \land P) \lor Q.$

Finally, by the commutative law, we have \[ (M \land P) \lor Q \equiv Q \lor (M\land P). \]

example.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Commutative Law

question.text: Simplify $(A \lor B) \lor A.$
question.explanation:
Using the commutative, associative, and idempotent laws, we get

\begin{align*} (A \lor B) \lor A &\equiv (B \lor A) \lor A \\[5pt] &\equiv B \lor (A \lor A)\\[5pt] &\equiv B \lor A. \end{align*}

example.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Commutative Law

question.text: Simplify $(A \lor B) \lor (C \lor B).$
question.explanation:
Using the associative, commutative, and idempotent laws, we get

\[ \begin{align*} (A \lor B) \lor (C \lor B) &\equiv (A \lor B) \lor (B \lor C) \\[5pt] &\equiv A \lor (B \lor B) \lor C \\[5pt] &\equiv A \lor B \lor C\\[5pt] &\equiv A \lor C \lor B\\[5pt] & \equiv (A \lor C) \lor B. \end{align*} \]

example.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Commutative Law

question.text: Which expression form is equivalent to $(Q \lor R) \land T?$
question.explanation:
By the commutative law, $Q \lor R \equiv R \lor Q.$

Therefore, $(Q \lor R) \land T \equiv (R \lor Q) \land T.$

example.title: Simplifying Symbolic Statements Using the Commutative Law

question.text: Which expression is equivalent to $X \lor (Y \land Z)?$
question.explanation:
By the commutative law, $Y \land Z \equiv Z \land Y.$

Therefore, $X \lor (Y \land Z) \equiv X \lor (Z \land Y).$
